domain: EU competition policy / state aid control (DG COMP case register)
prediction_question: At the instant the European Commission registers a state aid case (SA case number assigned on notification/registration, per the register's documented case fields), will the measure be handled under the ordinary/simplified procedure or will the Commission open a formal investigation under Article 108(2) TFEU before deciding?
prediction_time: The case's notification/registration date as published in the case record (to be verified in the JSON distribution's schema at the next probe). Features would be the fields fixed at notification: Member State, legal basis, aid instrument, sector, title text - all documented register fields; the decision-type/-date fields are post-hoc and must be excluded from features.
target_definition: Binary label derived from the case's decision record: a decision opening proceedings under Article 108(2) TFEU (formal investigation) vs decisions taken without opening (no-objection, block-exemption compatibility). Label source = the case's decision fields, excludable from features. Base rate unknown until the distribution is measured.

rejection_reason: PARKED on an ACCESS/evidence blocker (not on task shape): (1) LICENCE - the dataset-specific reuse instrument is unreadable from every vantage used: the data.europa.eu record's licence field is null, and every competition-cases.ec.europa.eu path returns a catch-all SPA shell (56,823 B) whose legal notice needs a JS browser; the EC general legal notice is not the dataset's own grant. Reopen when a dataset-specific reuse instrument is readable (e.g. the portal's legal-notice/about page read in the supported browser, or a licence field appearing on the portal record). (2) VINTAGE/LABEL COVERAGE - the measured notified-population filter (caseNotificationDate exists) returns 0 cases for initiation years 2025-2026 while the same index returns 3,862 and 3,106 SA cases for those years, so recent-vintage notification/decision coverage is not yet established; any split design must resolve this first (the 2015+ opening prevalence also collapses to ~0.3%, a regime property to design around). Novelty sweep not yet run; it becomes due only after (1) and (2) resolve.
review: Promising institutional-decision task in a procedure family this bench knows well (ec-merger-phase2-opening is published for merger control; state aid control is a different procedure, different population (SA.xxxxx cases, ~2 decades, tens of thousands of measures) and a different label). The cheapest unresolved fact that could change the verdict: whether the JSON distribution actually carries per-case row-level fields (registration date, legal basis, instrument, decision type/dates) with usable coverage, and what the Article 108(2)-opening base rate per year is. Second: the publisher's own licence instrument. A third check, novel to this family: the register is a live database, so historical vintages/as-of evidence for the case fields must be stated (case records carry their own decision dates, which mitigates, but feature-vintage claims need evidence).
next_action: PARKED until a reopening event. The ONE cheapest reopening probe, when the supported browser is available (a later discovery tick): open https://competition-cases.ec.europa.eu/ in the browser and read the dataset-specific legal-notice / about page (the plain-HTTP route is a catch-all SPA shell), quoting the licence/permission text into license_evidence. In the same session, resolve the recent-vintage coverage gap by measuring notification-date coverage in the JSON dump itself (ranged samples of caseNotificationDate across 2024-2026 vintages) rather than the search index, and sample the label-operand semantics for a handful of no-decision cases. Only after the licence is readable AND notification/decision coverage is measured for the intended split years: run scripts/check-novelty.py (state-aid decision prediction must be shown distinct from the published merger-control task and from DG COMP Scoreboard aggregate statistics), then reconcile the five discovery contracts and re-measure split windows on the dump vintage that construction will pin (the object is regenerated - lifecycle rule DeleteOldODPLogs, x-amz-expiration 2026-12-04 - so the build must pin its own digest). Construction, if it ever proceeds, stays in the standard order: construction -> full-worker qualification -> exact-byte acceptance -> reference/model scoring -> reporting.
